commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix chapter-wide composition gated the Brazil IEEPA surcharge carve-out on `entry_is_line_b` - a flag denoting the hand-built witness's single aluminum exemplar entry, an identifier that appears nowhere in the cited source - so the statutory aluminum carve-out to heading 9903.01.77 fired for exactly one entry line and the 40% Brazil duty was added to every other Section 232 aluminum article of Brazilian origin in chapter 98.
triage.triage_notes: Two distinct changes in this module diff. (1) SUBSTANTIVE: in both `ieepa_component_rate` (versions[0].formula, effective_from 2026-02-15) and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions`, `+ (if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b: brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate else: 0)` becomes `... and not entry_is_section_232_aluminum ...`. The unchanged proof atom on that formula is `corpus_citation_path: us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219`, `kind: exception`, excerpt 'The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02.' I read the corpus through resolve_provision.py: 9903.01.77 is the Brazil +40% IEEPA heading, 'Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90'; 9903.01.83 is the class-wide carve-out 'Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum; ...'; 9903.85.02 is 'products of aluminum provided for in the tariff headings or subheadings enumerated in subdivision (g) of note 19'. So the exception is defined by article class, not by one exemplar entry - the pre-fix condition is ungrounded and the fix re-grounds it. Kind is genuinely between untraceable_branch (condition with no source basis, re-grounded - matches the taxonomy's 'the fix removes or re-grounds it' and the PR's 'move from ... exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs') and wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out covers the wrong set of entries); I chose untraceable_branch, a reviewer may prefer the other. NOTE the post-fix gate excepts only aluminum, while 9903.01.83 also lists iron/steel and several other classes - a residual under-representation this commit does not address. (2) MECHANICAL: `ch98_s232_steel_heading_rate` and `section_232_steel_component_rate` only change the `source:` string and the proof atoms' corpus_citation_path from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; I compared parent and commit text - the rate stays '0.50', effective_from stays 2026-02-15, and the component formula is byte-identical. Provenance only, and it is corroborated: `us/statute/hts/9903.81.87` does not resolve in the pinned corpus at all (empty result) while `us/statute/hts/9903.82.02` resolves with exactly the recorded excerpt 'Rates of duty (1-General): The duty provided in the applicable subheading + 50%'. Classification for the module is driven by (1). Provenance/mechanism caveat for the corpus builder: these are generator-emitted `module.kind: composition` files - all 100 module diffs in this commit carry the identical pair of changes, and tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py at the PARENT commit already contained `"ieepa_component_rate": (("not entry_is_line_b", "not entry_is_section_232_aluminum"),)`, so the parent's committed YAML lagged its own generator and this commit is a regeneration sweep; only the steel citation was a fresh generator edit here. The committed pre-fix module content was still wrong against the source, so it is a usable fidelity item, but 100 near-identical copies should be deduped before benchmarking.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mechanical (the steel half of the diff is pure provenance: `ch98_s232_steel_heading_rate` keeps `formula: '0.50'` and only its `source:` string and two proof-atom citation paths move from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02), but the other two hunks change executable meaning in two rules' version formulas, so the module change is not provenance-only. The pre-fix chapter-wide composition gated the Brazil IEEPA surcharge carve-out on `entry_is_line_b`, which the same file uses as the caller-supplied exemplar flag standing in for the witness's single aluminum line (line 1925: `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` ... `formula: entry_is_line_b`); "line b" appears nowhere in the HTS, so the branch condition had no source basis while the rule's own unchanged proof atom claims the statutory exception ("The additional duties imposed by heading 9903.01.77 shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02"). I verified the carve-out is class-based, not line-based, through the pinned release: 9903.01.77 imposes +40% on Brazil "Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90", and 9903.01.83 covers "articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum" — so re-grounding the gate on `entry_is_section_232_aluminum` is exactly the untraceable-branch repair, not new coverage or a scope enhancement.
triage.verifier_quote:
-      + (if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b: brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate else: 0)
+      + (if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_section_232_aluminum: brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate else: 0)
triage.verifier_notes:
Kind check against alternatives: not polarity_or_logic (the `not` is unchanged; only the operand moved), not unrepresented_clause (the exception branch already existed pre-fix, wrongly predicated), not amount_mismatch (0.50 and brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate untouched), not wrong_period_or_effective_date (all effective_from unchanged). The runner-up is wrong_entity_or_scope (the carve-out reached the wrong population), but the decisive fact is that the predicate itself — a witness-fixture identifier — has no counterpart in the cited source and was re-grounded, which is the definition given for untraceable_branch.

Two cautions for the reviewer. (1) The first reader's quote is PR-level and mostly describes work not in this commit's ch98 diff: the "Section 232 steel component the witness never had" already exists in the parent (a9562cfd) — here it changes only by citation string — and adding it would in any case be new coverage, not a defect. The decisive evidence is the diff line, not that PR-body sentence. (2) The repair is partial: `entry_is_line_b` survives in the post file at line 1925 as the formula of `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded`, and 9903.01.83 also excludes iron/steel, copper, vehicles, semiconductors and wood products from the Brazil 40%, none of which the post-fix gate covers. That is residual under-coverage, not a reason to doubt that the pre-fix state was wrong.

Provenance note: resolving the cited atom's locator `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219` against the pinned corpus (release us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, corpus commit e79781bd) returns a Rev. 3 page of bare subheading numbers, not the quoted exclusion sentence — the same stale-locator-for-this-vintage pattern the commit report flags for 9903.81.x. The substantive exclusion is nonetheless verified directly at 9903.01.77 and 9903.01.83.
